LIF-R1 ST (question: Open → toUser → toUser again → the principal answers → answers again) {accepted: true}; still listed under the same offerId; the card stays open; a second toUser → expired; the later answer is accepted and is the call's result; the card closes; a further answer → already-settled
LIF-R1 ST (plan review: Open → toUser → the principal approves) {accepted: true}; still listed under the same offerId; the card stays open; the later approve is accepted: plan approved, plan mode off
LIF-R3 ST (question: Open → toUser → the user answers in the card) settlement {answered, by user, answers}; the result is the user's batch; the principal's later answer → expired or already-settled

LIF-R2 ST (Offered → escalate → escalate again → allow with risk high → allow) {accepted: true}; the stock prompt shows; still listed under the same offerId; a second escalate is refused; allow-needs-low-risk still applies; the valid allow is accepted, the call runs with the tool's own output and the prompt closes
LIF-R2 ST (Offered → escalate → reject with a reason) accepted; the call is rejected; the agent reads "The managing agent rejected this call: <reason>"; the prompt closes
LIF-R2 ST (Offered → escalate → the user clicks allowed-once first) the user's click decides; settlement {allowed, by user}; the principal's later allow → expired or already-settled
LIF-R2 ST (Offered → escalate → the user clicks rejected first) the user's click decides; settlement {rejected, by user}; the principal's later allow → expired or already-settled
LIF-R7 ST (question: handed to the user → silence) past a quiet period it is still listed under the same offerId, undecided, and the principal's answer then decides it
LIF-R6 ST (question: handed to the user → session_release) one retirement {released}; the user's own card decides the call
LIF-R6 ST (question: handed to the user → Take back) one retirement {released}; the user's own card decides the call
LIF-R6 ST (question: handed to the user → the principal's entry disabled) one retirement {revoked}; the user's own card decides the call
LIF-R7 ST (permission: handed to the user → silence) past a quiet period it is still listed under the same offerId, undecided, and the principal's answer then decides it
LIF-R6 ST (permission: handed to the user → session_release) one retirement {released}; the user's own prompt decides the call
LIF-R6 ST (permission: handed to the user → Take back) one retirement {released}; the user's own prompt decides the call
LIF-R6 ST (permission: handed to the user → the principal's entry disabled) one retirement {revoked}; the user's own prompt decides the call

LIF-R8 DT (a delegate passes → the manager escalates → the manager allows) a pass still reaches the manager as an offer; escalate keeps it listed; the manager's allow decides the call; no delegate settlement

LIF-R4 ST (a run_code program's ask: Open → its timeoutMs deadline while awaiting the ask → the principal answers → answers again) no retirement {withdrawn}; one notice {question-call-ended} correlated to the offerId saying it stays open; still listed; the answer is accepted and reaches the session as an answer_to_ended_question message; no settlement for it; a second answer → already-settled

LIF-R4 ST (a run_code program's ask: Open → it finishes with the ask unawaited → the principal answers → answers again) no retirement {withdrawn}; one notice {question-call-ended} correlated to the offerId saying it stays open; still listed; the answer is accepted and reaches the session as an answer_to_ended_question message; no settlement for it; a second answer → already-settled
LIF-R5 ST (question: Open → the user stops the turn) one retirement {withdrawn}; no notice; a late answer is refused
LIF-R5 ST (a run_code program's ask: Open → the user stops the turn) one retirement {withdrawn}; no notice; a late answer is refused
LIF-R5 ST (question: Open → the user dismisses the card) the call goes on with the dismissal; one retirement {withdrawn}; no notice; a late answer is refused
LIF-R5 ST (plan review: Open → the user's Discuss) one retirement {withdrawn}; no notice; a late approve is refused

EVT-UC-01 main 1 P opens subscriptions/listen on dsh-agent://events and gets the acknowledgement
EVT-UC-01 main 2 S1 asks a permission: the hint to P is sent by the time the commit resolves, and carries no event body
EVT-UC-01 main 3 P polls: one typed event with eventId, source session S1, correlation id = offer id and a bounded payload
EVT-UC-01 main 4 P acks with the receipt; a later poll does not return the event
EVT-UC-01 A1 P never subscribes: the same event is on its next poll
EVT-UC-01 A2 the hint is lost and the connector restarts: P re-listens, polls once and gets the event
EVT-UC-01 A3 P polls without acking: the event is returned again with the same identity, across a restart too
EVT-UC-01 E1 P polls with a cursor of another pair: forbidden
EVT-UC-01 E2 P polls with a stale cursor (older mailbox generation): explicit resync, never a silent skip
EVT-UC-01 E3 resources/read or subscribe on any other event URI: not found; no per-kind stream
EVT-UC-01 post P received all its events in order, each typed, unchanged (no interception for an external agent)
EVT-EP-02 row 1 the pair itself: poll, ack and the summary serve its own mailbox
EVT-EP-02 row 2 pair B reads dsh-agent://events: B's mailbox only, never A's events
EVT-EP-02 row 3 a pair-only access token: HTTP 403 insufficient_scope
EVT-EP-02 row 4 an ack naming another pair's eventId is unknown-event and acks nothing, not even the own receipt beside it
EVT-EP-02 row 5 an ack with a wrong payloadDigest is digest-mismatch and acks nothing
EVT-EP-02 row 6 the dsh-agent://events contents: {pending, headSequence, mailboxGeneration} only, never bodies
EVT-EP-02 row 7 answering an offer of another pair: forbidden
EVT-EP-02 row 8 an ack confers no answer authority: answering after the offer's revocation is refused
EVT-EP-04 row 1 an event committed to P's mailbox: one hint on its streams, nothing on the other pair's
EVT-EP-04 row 2 an event committed to Q's mailbox: one hint on its streams, nothing on the other pair's
EVT-EP-04 row 5 Q polls after an event to P: Q's mailbox has nothing of P's
EVT-EP-04 row 6 100 events to P in a burst: at least one hint, never more than one per commit, none to Q; none lost
EVT-BVA-01 row 1 0 pending, default limit: events [], hasMore false
EVT-BVA-01 row 2 1 pending, default limit: 1 event
EVT-BVA-01 row 3 LIMIT (100) pending, limit LIMIT: LIMIT events, hasMore false
EVT-BVA-01 row 4 LIMIT + 1 pending, limit LIMIT: LIMIT events, hasMore true; the next page gives 1
EVT-BVA-01 row 5 limit 0: refused limit-exceeded, never clamped
EVT-BVA-01 row 6 limit 101: refused limit-exceeded, never clamped
EVT-BVA-01 row 7 ordering: e1, e2, e3 committed are returned e1, e2, e3 with sequences one apart
EVT-BVA-02 row 1 max − 1 (199) queued automated events, then a message: queued
EVT-BVA-02 row 2 max (200) queued, then a message: queue-full to the caller, nothing queued, no hint
EVT-BVA-02 row 3 max queued, then a handover with the user's note: queued anyway (D§3.4)
EVT-BVA-02 row 4 max queued, one acked, then a message: queued
EVT-ST-01 row 1 (none) → commit → Pending: pollable, counted, one hint to the pair
EVT-ST-01 row 2 Pending → poll → Pending with the same identity
EVT-ST-01 row 3 Pending → ack with the correct digest → Acked: no longer pending
EVT-ST-01 row 4 Pending (contributed type) → contributor withdrawn → Retired: replaced by a retirement naming it
EVT-ST-01 row 5 Pending (offer type) → settled by the user → the offer event stays pending; the settlement follows it
EVT-ST-01 row 6 Pending (non-offer, ask included) → principal disabled → Held: kept across a restart, same identities
EVT-ST-01 row 6a Pending (offer type) → principal disabled → Retired: the offer's event is replaced and does not come back
EVT-ST-01 row 6b Pending Pending → principal deleted → Dropped; the dropped asks are returned, so their askers get unavailable
EVT-ST-01 row 6b Held Held → principal deleted → Dropped; the dropped asks are returned, so their askers get unavailable
EVT-ST-01 row 7 Held → entry re-enabled → Pending with the same identities
EVT-ST-01 row 8 Acked → ack again → Acked: a no-op success, counted as 0
EVT-ST-01 row 9 Acked → contributor withdrawn → Acked: it stays with the client, no retirement follows
K1-AMEND-1 row 1 (first use) (no storage) → first commit → a generation is set; every event and the summary carry it
K1-AMEND-1 row 2 (restart) a restart over the same storage is no loss: the generation is kept and a cursor from before pages
K1-AMEND-1 row 3 (hold, release) Pending → hold → release: the generation is kept; a cursor taken before the hold pages to the rest, same generation
K1-AMEND-1 row 4 (drop) Pending → drop (delete) → the generation is kept; a cursor from before pages (no resync) and reaches a later event

K1-AMEND-1 row 5 (hold expiry) Held → expireHolds(at) past MAILBOX.disabledRetentionMs → still held (forbidden), generation kept → release → a cursor from before pages (empty, no resync); a new commit carries the same generation
K1-AMEND-1 row 6 (storage lost) storage lost → a new generation; the new events carry it; an older cursor is resync with the current headSequence
K1-AMEND-1 row 6 (storage lost, nothing since) storage lost, nothing committed since: an older cursor is resync with the summary's headSequence, never an empty page
K1-AMEND-1 row 6 (foreign cursor) storage lost: another pair's cursor of the old generation is still forbidden, never resync
K1-AMEND-1 row 7 (pair isolation) dropping P keeps Q's generation too; Q's cursor still pages
K1-AMEND-3 row 1 (pending, namespace, tag) a pending contributed:<ns>.* event with the tag → retired as retire does (contributor-withdrawn, session and correlation kept)
K1-AMEND-3 row 1 (ack after) the retired event acked later → a no-op success counting 0
K1-AMEND-3 row 2 (acked) an acked event of that namespace and tag → left alone: no retirement names it
K1-AMEND-3 row 3 (other namespace) the same tag in another namespace (sharing the prefix) → left alone
K1-AMEND-3 row 4 (other tag) the same namespace, another activation's tag → left alone (a reload retires only the old activation)
K1-AMEND-3 row 4 (untagged) a contributor event committed with no tag → left alone
K1-AMEND-3 row 5 (non-contributed) other event types of the pair → left alone
K1-AMEND-3 row 6 (every pair) matching events in P's and Q's mailboxes → both retired, each retirement in its own pair's mailbox
K1-AMEND-3 row 7 (held) a matching event in a held mailbox → retired too: after release it is gone and its retirement is pending
K1-AMEND-3 row 8 (repeat) retireContributor twice → the second retires nothing new (one retirement per event)
K1-AMEND-3 row 8 (already retired) an event already retired by retire → no second retirement
K1-AMEND-3 row 9 (no match) a tag no event carries → nothing changes
K1-AMEND-3 row 10 (durable) the tag is stored with the event: after a restart retireContributor still finds it
K1-AMEND-3 EP 1 (never polled) a tagged contributor event as polled carries no activationTag
K1-AMEND-3 EP 2 (non-contributed) an activationTag on a non-contributed draft → commit throws TypeError; nothing committed
K1-AMEND-3 EP 3 (tag 42) a contributor draft whose activationTag is 42 (not a non-empty string) → commit throws TypeError; nothing committed
K1-AMEND-3 EP 3 (tag "") a contributor draft whose activationTag is "" (not a non-empty string) → commit throws TypeError; nothing committed
K1-AMEND-9 row 1 (pending, withdrawn) a pending event of the pair, reason withdrawn → {retired: true}; it is replaced by one retirement {retiredEventId, reason: withdrawn}
K1-AMEND-9 row 1 (pending, revoked) a pending event of the pair, reason revoked → {retired: true}; it is replaced by one retirement {retiredEventId, reason: revoked}
K1-AMEND-9 row 1 (pending, released) a pending event of the pair, reason released → {retired: true}; it is replaced by one retirement {retiredEventId, reason: released}
K1-AMEND-9 row 1 (pending, reissued) a pending event of the pair, reason reissued → {retired: true}; it is replaced by one retirement {retiredEventId, reason: reissued}

K1-AMEND-9 row 1 (pending, contributor-withdrawn) a pending event of the pair, reason contributor-withdrawn → {retired: true}; it is replaced by one retirement {retiredEventId, reason: contributor-withdrawn}
K1-AMEND-9 row 2 (acked) an acked event → {retired: false}; nothing committed, nothing changed; its receipt is still known
K1-AMEND-9 row 3 (already retired) retire twice → the first {retired: true}, the second {retired: false}; one retirement names it
K1-AMEND-9 row 3 (retired by retireContributor) an event retireContributor already retired → retire answers {retired: false}
K1-AMEND-9 row 4 (unknown) an event id no commit returned → {retired: false}; nothing changed
K1-AMEND-9 row 5 (another pair's) Q's pending event named under P → {retired: false}; Q's event stays pending, no retirement anywhere
K1-AMEND-9 row 6 (misuse) a principal key that is no string → retire throws (as before); nothing changed
K1-AMEND-9 ST 1 (Pending → ack → retire) Pending → ack → Acked → retire → {retired: false} (the ack/retire race seen from the mailbox)
K1-AMEND-9 ST 2 (Pending → retire → ack) Pending → retire {retired: true} → Retired → ack of its receipt → a no-op success counting 0; a second retire → {retired: false}
K1-AMEND-9 ST 3 (restart) a pending event survives a restart: retire after it → {retired: true}; an acked one after a restart → {retired: false}

UC: brief → claims → allow within scope; the judge sees purpose, scope, new messages and the request
EP: judged verdicts → allow, reject (a one-character reason is enough), pass with its reason, pass with an empty or no reason → bare pass
EP: JUDGE_FAILURE is exactly {timeout: judge-timeout, noAnswer: judge-no-answer, unreadable: judge-unreadable, failed: judge-failed}
DT: a failed judgement rejects with its JUDGE_FAILURE code, is logged, and neither stops the session nor emits drift
BVA: checkTimeoutSeconds — a judge that answers in time decides; one that does not → judge-timeout (logged)
ST: the caller's signal aborts while the judge runs → the rejection is that abort, not a JUDGE_FAILURE
DT: no active brief (not briefed / paused / briefed by a former manager) → bare pass; the judge is not asked
UC: the live sandbox case — the judge sees scope, command, danger-full-access and the sandbox rule; allow decides; a failing judge rejects with a JUDGE_FAILURE (not a pass)
DT: drift during a permission rejects the call, then stops the turn with TEXT.drift(permission, reason) and emits drift to the manager
ST: patrol — armed at brief; nothing new → no judgement; new messages → judged; drift → stop (TEXT.drift(patrol, reason)) + event; re-armed
ST: a patrol whose judgement fails (a throw, an unreadable answer) is logged and re-armed; nothing is stopped
ST: refine keeps the timer; pause stops the session with TEXT.paused, disarms and passes; resume re-arms
EP: tool refusals — not the manager, unbriefed, empty purpose, nothing to refine, briefed twice
DT: a subagent id briefs its root; a new manager neither inherits nor may use the old brief, but may brief again
EP: without the connector services Watchdog passes and refuses its tools
ST: briefs persist — a reopened store has them, and start() re-arms only unpaused ones
EP: a corrupt briefs file is logged and read as empty
EP: parseVerdict reads the first JSON object with a string verdict → {verdict, reason}; a non-string reason reads as ""
EP: parseVerdict → undefined for no object, invalid JSON, no verdict or a non-string verdict
